comment: F4 — promo addiction. The demo brand's committed three-cycle schedule (ticks 3-5, 8-10, 12-14 at 15/15/20%) over an 18-tick run, with the hero product 3000001 the only discounted item. The mechanism under test is the learned reference price: each window teaches a lower anchor via evidence.smooth_reference_price (alpha 0.3), so the full-price shelf afterwards reads as a LOSS and decide() row 13 doubles it. Needs real purchases to measure a share, so the population is the largest in the suite and goal arrivals are left at their configured rates. SIZED 2026-08-20: F4 measures a purchase SHARE across three promo windows, so it needs purchases in every window and between them — the one law here that cannot be rescued by a low-variance estimator. 500 shoppers plus a x8 arrival wave on 5504 across the whole run makes the population in-market; the promo schedule, not the arrival rate, is still the only thing that varies over time, so what the law measures is untouched.
